look_here_first: First decide annual or perennial, then inspect the stem wings. Common/fall sneezeweed is the perennial in this batch, with stout strongly winged stems and much broader obovate-to-lanceolate leaves that are often toothed. Its flower heads are also substantially larger than bitterweed's tiny heads.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: perennial herb, often 50–130 cm in FNA though local plants may be shorter; stems strongly winged by broad decurrent leaf bases; mid-stem leaves obovate to oblanceolate/lanceolate, much broader than H. amarum or H. elegans; leaf margins often dentate or remotely toothed, sometimes entire distally; upper plant strongly branched with many heads; heads relatively large, involucres globoid about 8–20 mm in FNA; yellow rays commonly 8–21 and 10–23 mm long; disc corollas 5-lobed; typically late-summer to fall flowering and associated with moist roadsides, streams, ditches, seepage areas and pond margins

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: Helenium amarum: H. amarum is an annual with unwinged stems, threadlike leaves and many tiny heads. Helenium elegans: H. elegans is annual and narrow-leaved; H. autumnale is perennial with broader often toothed leaves and larger heads. Helenium quadridentatum: H. quadridentatum is annual with narrow entire distal leaves and 4-lobed disc corollas; H. autumnale is perennial and 5-lobed in the disc.

lookalikes.differences: H. amarum is an annual with unwinged stems, threadlike leaves and many tiny heads. H. elegans is annual and narrow-leaved; H. autumnale is perennial with broader often toothed leaves and larger heads. H. quadridentatum is annual with narrow entire distal leaves and 4-lobed disc corollas; H. autumnale is perennial and 5-lobed in the disc.
